packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 11

Only this packet's prompt, metadata and supplied images were used. No identification, outside transcription, or catalogue context was consulted or exposed.

Layout survey
Both images are upright, with four narrow brown-ink columns arranged as two pairs separated by a broad central fold/gutter. A bifolium-like arrangement is visually plausible. The writing is small, cursive and heavily abbreviated. Severe mottled discoloration, abrasion, holes and ragged edge losses affect both faces. Mirrored holes suggest photographs of opposite sides of the same object. No clear running title, colored rubric, enlarged decorated initial, underlined lemma, or distinct marginal commentary can be identified. Slightly larger paragraph beginnings occur, but I cannot read them confidently. There is no trustworthy visual basis for separating main text and commentary.

Chosen areas and attempted samples
I selected the upper left column and the next column of image-001 because the upper ink is somewhat less damaged. I also checked image-002's upper left, which did not give a more reliable passage. No heading or question opening is readable enough to prioritize.

Columns A–D run left to right; physical lines are counted down from the first visible baseline in each column of the original image. Some counts remain approximate because fading obscures the first baseline. These are fragmentary, uncertain visual readings, not recovered passages.

Sample A:

These possible word groups are low-confidence and too generic to support a text match. I cannot responsibly provide two useful continuous samples from the supplied photographs. No proposed abbreviation expansions are supplied. No secure textual deletion or addition is discernible; dark patches are not treated as deliberate cancellation.

Transforms/inspection
Viewed both full images. image-001: 5000×4070 pixels; image-002: 5000×4060. Unmodified native crops examined: image-001 (450,264)–(1400,936); image-002 (450,263)–(1400,933); image-001 (1440,280)–(2340,1080). No rotation, filtering, contrast enhancement or restoration. Crops duplicate portions of the full images and are not independent witnesses.

Limitations/unread areas
The remaining columns and lower writing are untranscribed. Ink loss and surface mottling interfere with both letter identification and exact line counting. A different-light photograph, multispectral imaging or a specialist image-only reading is required before useful connecting prose can be offered. A larger view is already available and would not itself solve the ink-loss problem.
